title: Warehouse & Dispatch Assistant – Repair Centre
summary: Receive, log, pack and dispatch customer products at a service and repair centre in Taren Point. 35 hours per week, ongoing.
about: Unbox. Log. Pack. Ship. Customers send in their products for repair. You unbox them, scan them into the system and pass them to the technicians. Once they are fixed, you pack them up and send them back. If you have warehouse experience and like steady, hands-on work, this role is for you.

Our client is a global technology company with a range of consumer products sold in more than 80 countries. They are seeking a Warehouse & Dispatch Assistant to join their national Service team, based at their Service and Repair Centre in Taren Point.

Reporting to the National Service and Repairs Manager, you will manage the end-to-end process of receiving customer machines and parts, supporting technicians, and returning repaired products to customers. The role pays $35 per hour plus super for 35 hours per week, and is ongoing.
duties: Receive and unbox machines for service; log them in the CRM and service app and allocate them to technicians
Assist technicians with servicing and parts inventory
Pack, label (AusPost) and prepare repaired machines for dispatch
Maintain stock levels of packaging materials
Assist with production of refurbished products
Liaise with the Customer Service team on process and customer communications
Maintain a clean, safe work area in line with OH&S and company policies
reqs: Experience in a warehouse or goods receiving environment
Customer service experience
Methodical and able to manage your own workload to deadlines
Able to lift up to 18kg
Basic Microsoft Office skills
Forklift licence advantageous but not essential

Headquartered in Sydney, the company is undertaking a global supply chain transformation, establishing in-house and outsourced (3PL) hubs across Europe and Asia alongside its established ANZ operation. Revenue is approximately $150 million, and a private equity owner is investing heavily in technology and automation.

The Global Operations Director will integrate global logistics, warehousing and distribution, and build an operating model that supports current and future growth. The role includes oversight of the Australian distribution centre, where site managers are already in place.
duties: Set and deliver a global operations strategy aligned with the company's growth plans
Oversee global transport, warehousing and inventory management
Lead the Australian distribution centre on storage, handling, inventory accuracy and order fulfilment
Track KPIs and apply lean methods to reduce waste, lead times and cost
Drive automation and digital initiatives that improve data visibility and decision-making
Build, coach and lead a high-performing operations team
Own the operations budget and report performance to senior leadership
reqs: Degree in logistics, business or a related field; MBA or postgraduate qualification preferred
10+ years in global logistics or operations, including senior leadership
Experience running large-scale distribution centres
Track record of delivering strategic efficiency and growth initiatives
Strong command of logistics and warehousing technology
Analytical, data-led decision-maker with excellent stakeholder skills
